basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly define BBS; developmental delay 2/2. Proteinuria (1/1) and cardiac defect (1/1) omitted at cap; elevated liver enzymes alone do not establish damage.

decisions.renal: none: proteinuria in 1/1 supports possible renal involvement, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of defining skeletal features and developmental delay.
decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental and speech delay occur in 2/2 reported patients.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is a major BBS diagnostic feature and is documented in this subtype.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia with enlarged epiphyses and severe short stature; lens subluxation and cleft palate have no established frequency or major-criterion status in the supplied evidence.

decisions.ocular: none: lens subluxation is reported, but its frequency and status as a major diagnostic criterion are not established.

basis: Lower motor neuron degeneration defines the disease; progressive denervation causes actual skeletal muscle wasting and loss of function in essentially all patients.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: progressive denervation causes true skeletal muscle atrophy in essentially all patients, rather than weakness alone.

basis: Postinfectious immune inflammation; cardiac dysfunction occurs in roughly 40-60%. Inflammatory gastrointestinal involvement exceeds 30% and is a major diagnostic category; transient rash excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: inflammatory intestinal involvement is common (>30%) and a major diagnostic category; enterocolitis represents direct gut involvement.

basis: Cleft palate and intraoral adhesions define the disorder; mandibular hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement. Voice changes alone do not establish airway damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: micrognathia represents structural mandibular underdevelopment and is explicitly annotated as frequent (30-79%).

basis: Macroglossia/omphalocele, lateralized overgrowth and hyperinsulinism are defining; nephropathy is annotated 30-79%. Chorioretinal atrophy (30-79%) omitted at cap; tumor risk adds no axis.

decisions.ocular: none: chorioretinal atrophy is annotated 30-79% and would qualify, but is omitted at the four-axis cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized skeletal and muscular overgrowth is a cardinal diagnostic feature, beyond tall stature alone.

basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 5/5. Feeding difficulty (3/5) and constipation (2/5) do not establish direct gastrointestinal injury or intrinsic bowel dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: constipation in 2/5 and feeding difficulty in 3/5 establish symptoms, but not direct gastrointestinal damage or demonstrated intrinsic gut dysfunction.

basis: Inherited marrow failure; microphthalmia occurs in 8/22 (36%), and thumb/radial defects in roughly a third of Fanconi cases. Microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly in 14/22 (64%) is a head-size finding; the record does not establish associated brain malformation or neurologic impairment.

basis: NAD biosynthesis disorder with defining vertebral and renal malformations; cardiac defects each reported in 1/2. Speech delay (1/2) omitted at cap; cardiac tier reflects the three-primary limit.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypoplastic left ventricle and PDA each occur in 1/2; retained as the fourth axis under the three-primary limit.
decisions.renal: primary: renal hypoplasia/agenesis defines the syndrome; chronic kidney disease is reported in 1/2.
decisions.neurologic: none: speech delay in 1/2 supports involvement, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of metabolic, skeletal, renal and cardiac disease.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is a KYNU-related NAD biosynthesis disorder; elevated 3-hydroxykynurenine in 3/3 supports the metabolic defect.

basis: Peroxisomal disorder with defining neurologic dysfunction; hepatopathy and sensorineural hearing loss each commonly exceed 30%. Retinal degeneration also qualifies but is omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental neurologic dysfunction and progressive neurologic injury are defining features of Zellweger spectrum disorders.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal degeneration commonly exceeds 30%, but omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of neurologic, hepatic and hearing impairment.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss is a common intrinsic manifestation across the Zellweger spectrum, exceeding 30%.
